Commentary.Commentary: The new ball bowlers set the tone for the hosts! They kept it very tight and also got the big wicket of Stirling. Gwandu then continued the good work in the middle overs along with Wellington Masakadza. Raza was also handy throughout the middle and towards the end too the bowlers did a really good job. Zimbabwe have put themselves in a good position to clinch the series but they’ll need to bat well to chase this down. The wicket is not the easiest but not unplayable. Irish on the other hand need early wickets to put the hosts under pressure. An interesting second half follows.

They lost Stirling and Campher relatively early but Tucker and Andy Balbirnie put up a good partnership to steady things a little. Both though fell when it was time to up the ante and after that too, they kept losing wickets at regular intervals. Tucker however, along with Adair towards the end have managed to take them at 240.

A very fine effort with the ball by Zimbabwe and they’ll be the happier side heading into the break. Yes, the wicket is slightly on the slower side but we believe the Irish are slightly under par. They just couldn’t get going in this innings.
Leg bye! Angling on the pads. Adair misses his flick and it rolls on the deck for one. Ireland finish with 240/6.

TOSS - ZIMBABWE HAVE WON THE TOSS AND ELECTED TO FIELD!

Hello and welcome to the third and final ODI between Zimbabwe and Ireland. It's 1-1 right now and whoever wins takes the ODI series. Zimbabwe won the first game with Brian Bennett scoring a daddy hundred in front of the home fans. His innings made sure Zimbabwe defended down the total and won comfortably. Ireland though bounced back in style, Their bowlers came with a much more improved plan to keep Zimbabwe under 250. In reply, Stirling and Curtis Campher's fifty helped the visitors level the series. Ireland won the one-off test, will they clinch the ODI series as well or Zimbabwe will bounce back? Let's find out. Toss and team next.
...MATCH DAY...

The stage is set for the third and final ODI between Zimbabwe and Ireland at the Harare Sports Club. After Brian Bennett powered the hosts to victory in the series opener, Ireland hit back in style to level the series and set up a decider. A disciplined bowling performance saw the visitors restrict Zimbabwe to 245, and they chased it down comfortably with six wickets in hand and eight balls to spare. Unlike the first game, Ireland’s new-ball attack made an impact upfront, with Mark Adair leading the charge. He, along with Graham Hume, will once again be key in setting the tone with the ball. Josh Little has been quiet so far and will be eager to make his mark in this crucial clash. With the bat, Andy Balbirnie is yet to fire, but Paul Stirling, Harry Tector, and Lorcan Tucker have all chipped in, while Curtis Campher has delivered with both bat and ball. For Zimbabwe, batting proved to be their downfall in the second ODI, with multiple players failing to convert their starts. The bowlers, too, struggled for control, conceding as many as 23 extras. The hosts will need a collective effort from Brian Bennett, Craig Ervine, Wessly Madhevere, and Sikandar Raza, the latter two coming off fifties in the last game. With the ball, Richard Ngarava, Blessing Muzarabani, and Trevor Gwandu will have to deliver a more disciplined performance to keep Ireland in check. With the series on the line, both teams will be desperate to seize the moment and walk away with the trophy. Who are you backing to clinch the series?
